searchText: Here are my thoughts on the EIP-4444s discussion from today's call on whether we should bump the `eth` protocol version: https://notes.ethereum.org/M41Oj3WyRVSC36Rr0c-Tjg Let me know if there are any arguments that I've missed to account for or additional motivations for either side of the argument that I've missed. thanks for the summary Regarding EIP-7742, it says in the spec: > The Engine API is extended to provide both the target_blobs_per_block and the max_blobs_per_block when the CL requests the EL to construct a payload for proposal. I feel like the max_blobs_per_block there is unnecessary and can be removed since it is not being validated by EL anyway. Or am I missing something? i think we need the max to build the block? otherwise how will we know when to stop allowing blobs during creation? Rightt that would have been my next question, how to build the block 🙂 gotcha so we are disabling this check only when validating blocks. Does anybody have graphs of the max re-orgs depths over the last 6-12 months? I heard they should be extremely small and anything above a 7 block re-org would indicate something is wrong. But it would be useful to see the data if it is easily available. There was a discussion about this on github. I thought the conclusion was that sending `max_blobs_per_block` to EngineAPI's `new_payload` is redundant. https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3800#discussion_r1670341560 To be clear, the CL provides both `target_blobs_per_block` and `max_blobs_per_block` to the EL via `PayloadAttributes` here: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/electra/validator.md#execution-payload

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content:
Here are my thoughts on the EIP-4444s discussion from today's call on whether we should bump the `eth` protocol version: https://notes.ethereum.org/M41Oj3WyRVSC36Rr0c-Tjg

Let me know if there are any arguments that I've missed to account for or additional motivations for either side of the argument that I've missed.

excerpts.author: s1na
excerpts.content:
Regarding EIP-7742, it says in the spec:
> The Engine API is extended to provide both the target_blobs_per_block and the max_blobs_per_block when the CL requests the EL to construct a payload for proposal.

I feel like the max_blobs_per_block there is unnecessary and can be removed since it is not being validated by EL anyway. Or am I missing something?

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: i think we need the max to build the block? otherwise how will we know when to stop allowing blobs during creation?

excerpts.author: s1na
excerpts.content: Rightt that would have been my next question, how to build the block 🙂 gotcha so we are disabling this check only when validating blocks.

excerpts.author: kolbyml
excerpts.content: Does anybody have graphs of the max re-orgs depths over the last 6-12 months? I heard they should be extremely small and anything above a 7 block re-org would indicate something is wrong. But it would be useful to see the data if it is easily available.

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content:
There was a discussion about this on github. I thought the conclusion was that sending `max_blobs_per_block` to EngineAPI's `new_payload` is redundant.
https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3800#discussion_r1670341560

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content:
To be clear, the CL provides both `target_blobs_per_block` and `max_blobs_per_block` to the EL via `PayloadAttributes` here:
https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/electra/validator.md#execution-payload
